questions.q: What does the pipe operator | actually pass from the command on its left to the command on its right?
options: Only the plain text that would print to the console
The full object output, with all its properties — not just the text visible on screen
Nothing — | is purely a visual separator with no functional effect
A screenshot of the previous command's output
questions.explain: This is the concrete delivery of Lesson 1's claim: PowerShell's pipeline passes real objects, not text.

questions.q: Why does Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU work correctly?
options: Sort-Object secretly re-runs Get-Process internally
It doesn't actually work — Sort-Object cannot sort piped objects
CPU is a real property on the object being piped, not a column of text Sort-Object has to parse
CPU is a special reserved keyword unrelated to the process object
questions.explain: Because full objects flow through the pipe, Sort-Object can sort directly on the real CPU property.

questions.q: In Where-Object {$_.CPU -gt 100}, what does $_ refer to?
options: A fixed global variable that never changes value
The total count of objects in the pipeline
The name of the cmdlet being called
The current object flowing through the pipeline at that point, one at a time
questions.explain: $_ represents each object in turn as Where-Object evaluates the condition against it.

questions.q: When a pipeline filters objects with Where-Object, what happens to the properties on the objects that pass through?
options: The objects are converted to plain text before continuing
Every property is renamed automatically
All properties except the one being filtered on are deleted
They're untouched — filtering narrows which objects continue, it doesn't strip properties
questions.explain: Filtering only narrows which objects continue down the pipeline; each surviving object keeps its full set of properties.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to read a long, multi-stage pipeline?
options: All at once, without breaking it into stages
It cannot be read without running it first
Left to right, one stage at a time, asking what each stage receives and what it hands forward
Right to left, since PowerShell evaluates pipelines backwards
questions.explain: Reading left to right, stage by stage, turns even a long pipeline into a simple sequence of ordinary filters.
